summary: On the road to Jerusalem, Jesus tells the Twelve in detail that He will be betrayed, condemned, mocked, scourged, killed and raised the third day.
key_insight: Mark pictures Jesus walking ahead of the Twelve on the road up to Jerusalem while they followed, amazed and afraid. He was not being dragged to the cross; He was leading the way. And this time He told them more than ever before: the Gentiles, the mocking, the spitting, the scourging.
story: They were on the road, going up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was walking ahead of them. The disciples were amazed, and as they followed they were afraid. {Mk}

Once more He took the Twelve aside on the road {Mt} and began to tell them the things that would happen to Him. {Mk} “Behold, we are going up to Jerusalem, and all things that are written by the prophets concerning the Son of Man will be accomplished.” {Lk}

“The Son of Man will be betrayed to the chief priests and to the scribes; and they will condemn Him to death and deliver Him to the Gentiles.” {Mk} They would mock Him, insult Him and spit on Him, {Lk} scourge Him and crucify Him. {Mt} “And the third day He will rise again.”
But they understood none of these things. The saying was hidden from them, and they did not grasp what He was telling them. {Lk}
differences: Only Mark says Jesus was walking ahead of them and that the disciples were amazed and afraid.
Matthew alone names the cross: “to crucify.” Mark and Luke say they will “kill Him.”
Luke alone says that everything the prophets wrote about the Son of Man would be accomplished, and that the disciples understood none of it.
Luke does not mention the chief priests and scribes or the sentence of death; he begins with the handing over to the Gentiles.

scene.label: Going up
scene.text: Jerusalem stands high in the hills of Judea, so travelers always spoke of going up to it, whatever direction they came from. The Songs of Ascents (Psalms 120–134) were probably sung by pilgrims on the way to the feasts.

scene.label: Delivered to the Gentiles
scene.text: Under Roman rule the Jewish council could not carry out a death sentence on its own (John 18:31). To have Jesus killed, the leaders would need to hand Him to the Roman governor. Crucifixion was a Roman punishment, not a Jewish one.

scene.label: Scourging
scene.text: Roman flogging used a whip of leather straps, often weighted with pieces of bone or metal. It tore the skin and could kill. It commonly came before crucifixion.

scene.label: Spitting
scene.text: To spit in someone’s face was the deepest insult. Isaiah’s Servant says, “I did not hide My face from shame and spitting” (Isaiah 50:6). Both the council’s men and the Roman soldiers would do it (Mark 14:65; 15:19).

witnesses.matthew: Places the prediction right after the workers in the vineyard and right before the request for thrones. Matthew alone names the manner of death, “to crucify,” the plainest word in any of the predictions.
witnesses.mark: Paints the scene before the words: Jesus striding ahead, the disciples amazed and, as they followed, afraid. Mark lists each abuse in turn, and then sets James and John’s request for glory immediately after it.
witnesses.luke: Ties the suffering to Scripture: “all things that are written by the prophets.” Luke says three times over that the disciples did not understand, and after the resurrection Jesus opens their minds to these same prophets (Luke 24:25–27, 44–46).

seeing.reveals: Jesus walks toward the cross knowing every detail of it, and He walks in front. His death is not an accident of history but the fulfillment of what the prophets wrote, and He speaks of rising as surely as of dying.
seeing.living: Following Jesus means following someone who goes first into suffering. When His road frightens you, as it frightened the Twelve, remember that He is out in front, and that the third day is part of the same sentence.
seeing.ponder: Where is Jesus walking ahead of you on a road you are afraid to take?

preaching.big_idea: Jesus went to the cross on purpose, walking ahead of His frightened followers.
preaching.watch_for: In Mark each prediction is followed by the disciples missing the point: Peter’s rebuke (8:32), the argument about who is greatest (9:34), and now James and John’s request (10:35–37). Each time Jesus answers with a lesson on following and serving.

title: Jesus Foretells His Death a Third Time
